title: Zero conormal makes a square-zero closed immersion an isomorphism
statement: Let i:X → X′ be a first order thickening of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with square-zero kernel ideal sheaf I [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. If the tensor pullback i*I [def-pc-module-pullback] is the zero module, then i is an isomorphism. No affine, finite type or universal-property assumption is required.

proof.text: For each affine open U in X′, use affine_conormal_sections with R=Γ(X′,U), the identity coordinate equivalence and I=ker(i.app U). This gives I/I² ≃ Γ(i*I,i⁻¹U).

The identity of the zero conormal module is the zero morphism; evaluating on sections forces every section to be zero. The equivalence therefore makes I/I² subsingleton. Ideal.cotangent_subsingleton_iff gives I²=I. Evaluating the first order hypothesis on U gives I²=0, hence I=0. These are the definitions of the quotient module and square-zero ideal.

IdealSheafData.ext on all affine opens now gives i.ker=bottom. IsClosedImmersion.isIso_iff_ker_eq_bot (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean:198) proves that i is an isomorphism. This is the closed-immersion zero-kernel criterion.

theorem firstOrderThickening_isIso_of_conormal_isZero {X X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (hC : IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules)) :
    IsIso i
